newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai PM says Amnuay to stay as finance minister.
newsitem.headline: Thai PM says Amnuay to stay as finance minister.

text.p: Thai prime minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh reiterated on Tuesday there will be no change in economic ministers and Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan will continue in his post.
"Amnuay will still have authority in economic affairs and there will be no change in the economic ministers," Chavalit said after a weekly cabinet meeting.
His comments follow renewed speculation that Amnuay was due to resign following a conflict with a major partner in Chavalit's coalition.

On Monday, Amnuay also dismissed market speculation that the Chart Pattana Party, a major coalition party in the government, was unhappy with his performance during the administration's six months in office.
Some members in Chavalit's government suggested late last week that Amnuay could help halt the Thai economic slowdown and a prolonged stock market decline by stepping down.
Chavalit has said he would follow financial affairs more closely from now on.

The prime minister also said the country's macroeconomic fundamentals would improve this year and said projected gross domestic product (GDP) growth of about five to six percent in 1997 was not that bad.
"We have had high economic growth for the past 10 years so there must be some overheating and adjustment," he said.
Private analysts said the Thai economy is expanding about five percent this year, its slowest pace in a decade.
Chavalit repeated comments made by other government officials that the current account deficit should come in around six percent of GDP this year, compared to 8.2 percent in 1996.
He said the government would try to balance the budget by cutting spending or lifting revenues by raising luxury taxes.
